description: E. algoensis is variable especially in leaf-shape but has always flat and rather broad leaves which are more or less distinctly cuneate. Two different leaf-types are shown in, one apically three-toothed leaf and one more dissected, pinnatilobate leaf. All gradations between these extremes occur. The minute glands on the leaf-margins are sometimes very sparse or absent.
bibliographicCitation: Nordenstam, RB. 1968. The genus Euryops I. Opera Bot. 20: 7-409. [All rights reserved]

description: O. bidens is a perennial herb, with narrow, erect, furrowed stems, striate in the upper part. The younger specimens of this plant are clothed with a white, cobweb-woolly indument. The older, on the other hand, have almost entirely lost their hairy covering and their lower leaves, so that the appearance of the plant has changed considerably.The achenes in O. bidens are more or less conspicuously 3-angled. the two outer angles being 2-3-tubercled, the inner one smooth, blunt, and usually very slightly prominent. The apex is truncate and 3-corªnered, with one blunt tubercle in each corner. Besides these achenes of normal appearance, an achene with a considerably aberrant form may occasionally occur in a head.
bibliographicCitation: Norlindh, NT. 1943. Studies in the Calenduleae: 1. Monograph of the genera Dimorphotheca, Castalis, Osteospermum, Gibbaria & Chrysanthemoides. C.W.K. Gleerup, Lund. [All rights reserved]

description: Osteospermum amplectens is an annual, glandular-puberulous herb, characterized by its small triangular-pear-shaped, 3-winged achenes, only 4-5 mm long. They have a small but, as a rule, clearly developed apical cavity, c. 0.5 mm in diam., but it is not provided with fenestrae, as in most of the other species in the subgenus Tripteris (with the exception of O. breviradiatum and O. tomentosum), being surrounded by an impellucid pericarp of subequal thickness. In each head c. 20 winged achenes develop. Nearly every head contains besides one or occasionally two wingless, terete, slightly incurved achenes, c. 10 mm long, produced into a beak. The flower heads are yellow to orange with a dark disc, and when fully expanded measure up to 5 cm in diam. The ray flowers are about 3 times longer than the involucre.
bibliographicCitation: Norlindh, NT. 1943. Studies in the Calenduleae: 1. Monograph of the genera Dimorphotheca, Castalis, Osteospermum, Gibbaria & Chrysanthemoides. C.W.K. Gleerup, Lund. [All rights reserved]

description: Involucral bracts densely or sparsely silky-hairy on the margins, sometimes only in the lower part Involucral bract margins also with coarse triangular glands Capitula in a large secondary head In fresh specimens the ray florets of O. capensis are dark yellow to orange compared to the bright yellow florets in O. imbricata.
bibliographicCitation: Koekemoer, M. 2017. Key to the southern African species of the Relhania and Macowania groups in the Gnaphalieae (Asteraceae). https://keyserver.lucidcentral.org/key-server/data/04040f0a-0603-4405-880c-010703060006/media/Html/default.html [All rights reserved]

description: This species forms a transition between the shrubby species of the section and those with annual stems from a subterranean caudex. E. pedunculatus sometimes develops to a vigorous branching shrub somewhat resembling E. abrotanifolius in habit. In other cases the stems are short, little-branched and suffrutescent, arising from a thick subterranean caudex. Such forms have much resemblance to E. laxus. It is not known whether a subterranean caudex is always developed, but it is present in all material seen with preserved basal parts. E. pedunculatus is an extremely variable species. The considerable variation in habit is mentioned above, and the variation in leaf-shape and length of rays is equally striking. A local population from the Kaapsche Hoop area in eastern Transvaal has been described as E. rogersii. It has a characteristic appearance, being a vigorous shrub with small, pinnatipartite leaves, but it seems to be connected with more typical pedunculatus by a continuous series of transitional forms in the surrounding areas. Forms with short and only weakly lignified stems are not so easily defined against E. laxus, which is obviously quite closely related. Distinguishing characters are the less connate and more overlapping involucral bracts and the more densely pubescent and usually smaller achenes of E. pedunculatus.
bibliographicCitation: Nordenstam, RB. 1968. The genus Euryops I. Opera Bot. 20: 7-409. [All rights reserved]

description: The well crisped, denticulate, somewhat squarrose involucral bracts and long fimbrils on the receptacle, together with generally simple stems without axillary leaf tufts, characterize the species. Specimens from Katberg and the Amatola Mountains often have numerous short branches arising near the base of the flowering stems and very narrow acuminate leaves, but do not differ otherwise.
