description: Intermediates between I. disticha and I. leptocarpa Eckl. & Zeyh. occur in the Elandsberg region and sometimes I. disticha approaches I. leptocarpa morphologically in the Sneeuberg and Graaff-Reinet Districts, making unifoliolate forms of I. disticha difficult to tell apart from I. leptocarpa.
bibliographicCitation: Boatwright, JS; et al. 2019. Fabaceae. In: CL Bredenkamp (ed.), A Flora of the Eastern Cape Province, Strelitzia 41(2): 926-1066. South African National Biodiversity Institute, Pretoria. [CC BY]

description: A shrub 3-4 ft. high, allied to I. sordida Benth., but differing in having an eglandular calyx.
bibliographicCitation: Baker, EG. 1926. The leguminosae of Tropical Africa. Erasmus, Ghent. [All rights reserved]

description: Stem 2-3 feet high, erect, quite simple, rigid and rod-like, closely imbricated with leaves. Pubescence copious, whitish, soft, short, patent. Leaves 1-1.25 inch long, erect. Leaflets 4-5 lines long, 1-2 lines wide, obtuse, somewhat cuneate at base. Peduncles very patent, 2-3 inches to the base of the dense raceme, which is 4-5 inches long; pedicels much longer than the calyx. Flowers rather small (withered only seen). Legumes1.5-1.75 inch long, quite straight.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: A. cultriformis differs from A. podalyriifolia in being glabrous and in having narrower pods.
bibliographicCitation: Ross, JH. 1975. Mimosoideae, Fl. S. Africa 16(1): 1-155. BRI, Pretoria. [CC BY]

description: Many-stemmed, 12-14 inches high, chiefly branched from the base; branches erect and subsimple. Leaves about an inch apart; leaflets 1/2-3/4 inch long, 1-2 lines wide, the terminal shortly petioled. Peduncles 5-6 inches long, after flowering becoming very rigid. Flowers closely crowded, pinky-purple, 3 lines long. Legumes 1-11 inch long, slightly rugulose, 12-14 seeded. The whole plant is very pale, whitish- green, harsh to the touch and rigid.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Indigofera evansii is allied to I. dimidiata Walp., but is easily distinguished by its small and narrow stipules, up to 2 mm broad near the base (not at least 4 mm) and obovate-cuneate leaflets (not lanceolate to elliptic). The narrow stipules also distinguish it from I. mollis Ecklon & Zeyher which it most resembles in leaf shape. It has much the aspect of I. procumhens L. from the SW Cape, but it is a much more delicate-looking plant as Schlechter himself noted: the runners are above ground (not subterranean), the peduncle thin (not thick and fleshy at the base), inflorescence rather lax (not rather dense), standard glabrous on the back (not spreading-pubescent), keel obtuse, glabrous on midline (not acute, spreading-pubescent on midline). I. evansii is also very closely allied to I. pseudoevansii described below.
bibliographicCitation: Burtt, BL; Hilliard, OM. 1986. Notes on some plants of southern Africa chiefly from Natal: XII. Notes Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinburgh 43(2): 189-228. [CC BY-SA]

description: Cultivated for dune reclamation, firewood, invades dunes, watercourses, roadsides, fynbos; origin Australia, declared invader (Category 2).
bibliographicCitation: Boatwright, JS; et al. 2019. Fabaceae. In: CL Bredenkamp (ed.), A Flora of the Eastern Cape Province, Strelitzia 41(2): 926-1066. South African National Biodiversity Institute, Pretoria. [CC BY]

description: A strong, erect, much branched and ramulous, densely leafy bush, with the habit of I. sulcata, to which it is nearly allied, but from which it differs in the rameal pubescence, shape of leaflets, calyx and legume. Petioles 1-2 lines long. Leaflets cuneate at base, gradually widening upwards, flat or nearly so, 3-5 lines long, 1-1.5 wide near the blunt extremity. Racemes 4-5 flowered; pedicels 2 lines long. Calyx-teeth very short, bluntish. Flowers rosy purple, 2 lines long. Legumes 4-5 lines long, densely clothed with microscopic, white pubescence.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Common petiole uncial, the pairs of leaflets 2 lines apart. Leaflets 4-5 lines long, more or less concave. Racemes 0.75 inch long; pedicels filiform, at length 3-4 lines long. Flowers 2 lines long, tawny externally. Legumes 0.5 inch long. The very erect leaves, much longer petiole, and more distant pairs of leaflets, the terminal sometimes petioled, and the short legumes distinguish this from I. stricta.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Cultivated for shelter, firewood, construction, invades grassland, river courses; origin Australia, declared weed (Category 1).
bibliographicCitation: Boatwright, JS; et al. 2019. Fabaceae. In: CL Bredenkamp (ed.), A Flora of the Eastern Cape Province, Strelitzia 41(2): 926-1066. South African National Biodiversity Institute, Pretoria. [CC BY]

description: Rather variable in aspect; 12-20 inches long, more or less ligneous, and more or less erect or diffuse: but recognisable by its pale green foliage, the leaves very patent and distant, rigid pubescence, and long, subspicate racemes of small, canescent flowers. Leaves 1-2 inches apart: the common petiole robust, 0.5-0.45 inch long. Leaflets varying from 3 to 7 lines long, and from narrow-obovate to lanceolate-linear. Raceme occupying 0.75 of the peduncle, which is eventually 6-7 inches long. Legumes 1-1.5 inch long.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: E. burkei differs from E. elephantina primarily in being a shrub or tree with branched perennial aerial stems and not a suffrutex with annual unbranched aerial stems (unless damaged). The leaflet-base in E. burkei is less asymmetric than in E. elephantina, and the midrib soon becomes ± centric. The leaflets of E. burkei are typically larger than those of E. elephantina. E. burkei appears to have smaller seeds than E. elephantina, but more fruiting material is required to confirm this.
bibliographicCitation: Ross, JH. 1975. Mimosoideae, Fl. S. Africa 16(1): 1-155. BRI, Pretoria. [CC BY]

description: A slender, laxly branched, more or less albescent suffrutex, varying in the breadth of its leaflets and the length and fertility of its racemes; but the varieties are scarcely definite, and all grow together. The var. with its pulvinate tufts of brown glands between the leaflets looks distinct; but some of Drège’s specimens have these glands, and others want them. Zeyher's 2429, from the Zwartkops, is a more glabrous form, with laxer and larger foliage, and remarkably long peduncles; it probably grew in a very wet, perhaps shady situation.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Allied to I. hilaris E. and Z. but readily distinguished by its dwarf habit, much smaller calyx and much larger corolla.
bibliographicCitation: Brown, NE. 1925. New species of Indigofera from the Transvaal and Swaziland. Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1925(3): 142-159. [https://www.jstor.org/stable/4118659] [All rights reserved]

description: A slender, prostrate plant, with stems 12-18 inches long, alternately much branched. Petioles 1-2 lines long. Leaflets 3-4 lines long, 1-1.5 line wide, pale green, rough with short, patent hairs. Peduncles in flower scarcely uncial, in fruit 1.5 inch long. Legumes 3-4 lines long. This has the look of a small trefoil. It is near I. incana, but differs in its much smaller and narrower stipules, shorter, few- flowered racemes, hairy petals, and very small, few-seeded legumes.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Stems ligneous but slender, 1-2 feet long, with ascending, subvirgate, 4-angled branches. Petioles 2-3 lines long. Leaflets 4-5 lines long, sometimes very narrow, sometimes 2 lines wide beyond the middle, always tapering at base, subobtuse or acute; the pubescence scanty on the upper, copious on the lower surface. Peduncles 4-6 inches long; racemes dense, elongating; pedicels 1 line long. Legumes 0.5-0.75 inch long.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: 1-3 feet high, suffruticose or quite shrubby, robust and much-branched: the whole plant clothed with spreading, whitish, rather rough, short hairs. Leaves densely crowded on the more shrubby specimens, patent; the common petiole 2.5-3 inches long. Leaflets horizontal, variable in width and in the bluntness and acuteness of the ends, about 0.5inch long. Spikes nearly twice as long as the leaves, cylindrical, hairy. Flowers purple, 3-4 lines long. Legumes not 0.5 inch long, 3-4 seeded.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: A tall, strong, leafy shrub; the younger parts microscopically silky, the older becoming glabrous, and pale, blueish-green. Common petiole 2-4 inches long, the pairs of leaflets 0.5-0.75 inch apart, the terminal at least 0.25 inch beyond the last pair. Leaflets 0.5-0.75 inch long, 4-6 lines wide, thickish, flat, with wholly immersed or obsolete veins. Racemes elongating, the flowers 2-3 lines apart on pedicels 2-3 lines long. Calyx remarkably open and subtruncate, repand-toothed. Legumes 1.5-1.75 inch long, somewhat 4-angled, with very convex valves, spongy and chambered within, wrinkled.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: A. dealbata is sometimes confused with A. mearnsii. It differs from the latter in lacking the glands in between the pinnae pairs along the upper surface of the leaf-rhachis, in being more pruinose, and in having wider usually less moniliform pods.
bibliographicCitation: Ross, JH. 1975. Mimosoideae, Fl. S. Africa 16(1): 1-155. BRI, Pretoria. [CC BY]

description: E. burkei differs from E. elephantina primarily in being a shrub or tree with branched, perennial, aerial stems and not a suffrutex with annual, unbranched, aerial stems (unless damaged). The leaflet- base in E. burkei is less asymmetric than in E. elephantina, and the midrib soon becomes ± centric. The leaflets of E. burkei are typically larger than those of E. elephantina. E. burkei appears to have smaller seeds than E. elephantina, but more fruiting material is required to confirm this.
bibliographicCitation: Ross, JH. 1974. The genus Elephantorrhiza. 11(3): 247-257. [All rights reserved]

description: A woody and twiggy, pale grayish small shrub. Leaves densely set. Common petiole 1-1.5 inch long, the pairs of leaflets 2 lines apart. Stipules 1-2 lines long, remarkably patent. Leaflets 3-4 lines long, 1.5 line wide, greyish. Racemes subsessile, 8-10 flowered; scarcely an inch long.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Differs from I. stenophylla, E. & Z., by the broader and longer canescent-strigillose obtuse leaves and the more densely (10-15) flowered racemes.
bibliographicCitation: Fourcade, HG. 1932. Contributions to the flora of the Knysna and neighbouring divisions. Trans. Roy. Soc. South Africa 21(1): 75-102. [All rights reserved]

description: This is very similar to I. hilaris E. and Z. in general appearance, although readily distinguished by the presence of stalked glands upon its stems and leaflets. It is probably a hybrid between I. hilaris and one of the species having gland-tipped setae.
bibliographicCitation: Brown, NE. 1925. New species of Indigofera from the Transvaal and Swaziland. Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1925(3): 142-159. [https://www.jstor.org/stable/4118659] [All rights reserved]

description: Stems 1-2 feet long, terete, slender, subsimple, or branched near the base, probably prostrate, the habit resembling that of a Tribulus. Leaves 1-1.5 inch long; leaflets 4-5 lines long, 2-3 lines wide. Flowering peduncles 3, fruiting 5 inches long; flowers small, subsessile. Legumes 4-5 lines long. Every part of the plant is clothed with dense, white, appressed, short bristles, by which character and the more diffuse habit it is known from I. alternans.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: A slender, glabrous and very pale, yellowish-green, almost herbaceous species; erect according to E. Meyer, but the specimen from Drège, in Hb. Benth. has the same trailing habit of those of Ecklon and Zeyher, from which our description is more especially drawn. Common petiole 1.5-3 inches long, the first pair of leaflets at least 0.75 inch from the base, the rest 2-3 lines apart. Leaflets 3-4 lines long, obtuse or acute, sometimes almost lanceolate. Peduncles 6-8 inches long, in fruit erect; pedicels 1-2 lines long. Legumes 1.25 inch long, subtorulose, dark brown.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Tap-root subsimple, slightly fibrous. Stems many from the crown, 1-2 feet long, spreading over the soil in all directions, much or little branched, roughly hairy. Petioles 2-3 lines long. Leaflets 3-7 lines long, 2-4 lines wide, palish green, obtuse or subacute. Peduncles 3-6-8 inches long, ending in a short raceme of several purple, dark-tipped, nearly glabrous flowers. Corolla 2.5 lines long. Legume 1-1.5 inch long, densely but shortly hispid. Varying in the size of leaf, length of peduncle, but generally known by its pubescence and stipules. Burchell's 5108 has narrower stipules than usual.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Very closely allied to I. frutescens Linn. f. and perhaps only a stunted form of that species, but the leaflets besides being much smaller are broader in proportion to their length, being sometimes almost orbicular and are more closely set, and the flowers are smaller.
bibliographicCitation: Bolus, H. 1915. Novitates Africanae. Ann. Bolus Herb. 1: 126-133. [All rights reserved]

description: A small, angularly-branched plant, 6-8 inches long. Petioles 1.5-2 lines long. Leaflets 3-5 lines long, rigid, subglaucous. Peduncles (in fruit only seen) 1-1.5 inch long. Legume brown, 6-7 lines long, not a line wide. Differs from I. complicata, in the short petioles, stipules, racemes, legumes. The foliage is not dissimilar; the pubescence much more scanty.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Intermediates between I. leptocarpa and I. disticha Eckl. & Zeyh. occur in the Elandsberg region.
bibliographicCitation: Boatwright, JS; et al. 2019. Fabaceae. In: CL Bredenkamp (ed.), A Flora of the Eastern Cape Province, Strelitzia 41(2): 926-1066. South African National Biodiversity Institute, Pretoria. [CC BY]

description: This species is well distinguished by the terminal leaflet being very much longer than the others.
bibliographicCitation: Brown, NE. 1925. New species of Indigofera from the Transvaal and Swaziland. Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1925(3): 142-159. [https://www.jstor.org/stable/4118659] [All rights reserved]

description: Cultivated as ornamental, shelter, invades forest clearings, fynbos, urban areas; origin Australia, declared invader (Category 3).
bibliographicCitation: Boatwright, JS; et al. 2019. Fabaceae. In: CL Bredenkamp (ed.), A Flora of the Eastern Cape Province, Strelitzia 41(2): 926-1066. South African National Biodiversity Institute, Pretoria. [CC BY]

description: Densely tufted 6-8 inches high, slightly woody at base. Leave3 closely set, much longer than the internodes. Petioles 4-5 lines long. Leaflets 1.5-2 inches long, 1-3 lines wide, tapering much to each end, a dull, rusty brown externally, with prominent veins. Stipules 3/4-1 inch long, brown. Peduncles 5-8 inches long, the upper half floriferous. Flowers pinky-crimson, 3 lines long. Allied to I. cuneifolia, but less woody, with much narrower and longer leaflets and stipules.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: A single specimen, without flower or fruit, exists in Hb. Ecklon, now Dr. Sonder’s. It seems to be a rigid, strong growing, divaricate, and sparsely leafy shrub, thinly canescent in all parts, and ashen-grey. The branches 8-12 inches long, are very rigid and straight. Leaves 5 inch apart, 4-5 lines long, 3 lines wide, retuse or deeply emarginate, many of them exactly heart-shaped, the midrib obvious on the upper, and prominent on the under surface. No appearance of inflorescence, save very young flower-buds.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: A stunted plant, with thick, much branched, depressed woody stems and ascending slender branches. Leaves laxly set, 1-1.5 inch long. Leaflets pale green, 5-6 lines long, 1 line wide, expanded. Peduncles rarely as long as the leaves; flowers rosy, on longish pedicels, the vexillum brownish behind. Bracts subpersistent, 1/4 line long. Flowers 3 lines long. Legumes 1-11/4 inch long, not a line wide.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Procumbent or depressed, much-branched, with copious, soft, pale pubescens. Leaves 1.5 inch long, of several pair, the lowest pair near the base of the common petiole. Leaflets 4-5 lines long, 2-3 lines wide, green and nearly glabrous above, fulvous and softly hairy beneath. Peduncles 2-3 inches long, the upper half floriferous. Flowers purple, 3 lines long. Legumes about 8 seeded, 1/2 inch long, or rather more, with a hard, sharp, black point.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: The whole plant is thinly, but rigidly, strigose, with appressed, white, middle-fixed hairs. Common petiole scarcely inch long; the pair of leaflets 2 lines apart. Leaflets 2.5-3 lines long, 1-1.5 line wide, flat. Raceme 5-8 flowered, 1-1.5 inch long; peduncle setaceous. Flowers 2 lines long. Unripe legume 4 lines long, 0.5 line wide.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Leaflets pale green, elliptic, apex acute, base cuneate. Stipules slightly prolonged truncate appendages in seedlings, soon reverting to auriculate lobes on both sides, and sharply reflexed as in V. richardsiae and V. triphylla; pulvinous action apparent in seedlings. Stems deeply grooved to winged. Style with beak present as a short semi-erect, rounded 'fingertip' or 'thimble'-like projection within the short-rostrate keel. Legumes erect, paired, up to 60 mm long, obtusely beaked, 14-seeded. Seeds small, almost spherical, 3 x 2 mm, with aril scarcely developed.
bibliographicCitation: Pienaar, BJ. 1991. A new species of Vigna Savi (Fabaceae) from southern Africa. S. African J. Bot. 57(6): 314-318. [Copyright held by the South African Association of Botanists (1991); http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/journal/02546299] [CC BY]

description: A rigid shrub, nearly allied to I. spinescens.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Cultivated for shelter, firewood, construction, ornamental tree, invades grassland, river courses, roadsides; origin Australia, declared invader (Category 2).
bibliographicCitation: Boatwright, JS; et al. 2019. Fabaceae. In: CL Bredenkamp (ed.), A Flora of the Eastern Cape Province, Strelitzia 41(2): 926-1066. South African National Biodiversity Institute, Pretoria. [CC BY]

description: The leaflets are both shorter and narrower than those of A. robustum. In addition, plants of A. speciosum are smaller and much less floriferous than A. robustum. A correlated trend occurs in the peduncle development which is accentuated in A. speciosum allowing its flowers to be held above the surrounding vegetation despite its reduced vegetative stature. A strong tendency towards leaf dimorphism is also apparent in A. speciosum, with broad lower leaflets and narrow upper leaflets.
bibliographicCitation: Edward, TJ. 1997. Notes on Argyrolobium (Fabaceae) in South Africa. S. African J. Bot. 63(5): 271-275. [Copyright held by the South African Association of Botanists (1997); http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/journal/02546299] [CC BY]

description: The distinguishing features of this plant are: The erect stems covered with tawny hirsute pubescence. The imparipinnate leaves with often about 6 pairs of ovate, or somewhat obovate leaflets.
bibliographicCitation: Schinz, H. 1904. Beiträge zur Kenntniss der Afrikanischen Flora (XVII). Vjschr. Naturf. Ges. Zürich 49: 171-196. [https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/35455#page/197/mode/1up] [All rights reserved]

description: A small, woody, dwarf, spreading shrub, 6-12 inches long, hoary with long hairs, which fall off from the older leaves. Petioles 1-2 lines long. Leaflets 3-4 lines long, 2 lines wide, with a sharp, brown mucro. Stipules much acuminate, twice as long as the petiole or longer. Racemes 3-5 flowered, woolly. Flowers small. Legumes 3-4 lines long, very woolly. Sometimes confounded with I. coriacea, var. hirta, and sometimes with I. sarmentosa, but very distinct from either.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Differs from I. flabellata, Harv., by the revolute margins of the leaflets, by the woolly, not strigose, pubescence, and by the setaceously acuminate calyx lobes.
bibliographicCitation: Fourcade, HG. 1932. Contributions to the flora of the Knysna and neighbouring divisions. Trans. Roy. Soc. South Africa 21(1): 75-102. [All rights reserved]

description: Pod 3-4 mm wide, yellow to greyish-brown.
bibliographicCitation: Schrire, BD. 2012. 61. Leguminosae (Papilionoideae): Tribe 7. Indigofereae, Fl. Zambes. 3(4): 1-245. Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, London. [CC BY]

description: This is very similar to I. galpinii N.E. Br. but differs by its lfts. being broader (3-7 mm. instead of 2-4 mm.) and more elliptic, the bud part of the raceme 4 mm. (instead of 2-3 mm.) br., the lower fls. 2-5 mm. (instead of 5-10 mm.) apart, and the pubescence on the standard in bud very dark brown, instead of golden brown.
bibliographicCitation: Burtt Davy, J. 1932. A manual of the flowering plants and ferns of the Transvaal with Swaziland, South Africa. Longmans, London. [All rights reserved]

description: A very scraggy, intricately branched, robust, spiny and sparsely leafy bush; the younger parts canescent with short, silky, appressed hairs. Leaflets 2-4 lines long, the upper surface, except of the young leaflets, mostly glabrous. Racemes in fruit sometimes uncial, in flower much shorter. Flowers small. Legumes 4-8 lines long, 2 lines wide, strongly falcate.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Stem one or two feet high; the whole plant densely clothed with long, soft, pale hairs. Leaves 1.5 - 2 inches long, closely set. Leaflets 4-6 lines long, 2-3 lines wide. Flowers small, closely set, subsessile, on peduncles 4-6 inches long. Legumes strongly deflexed, imbricating, very hairy with dark or blackish hairs.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: This species is also allied to that which in the Flora Capensis, vol. ii, p. 196, is described under the name I. seticulosa, Harv.,which I take this opportunity of pointing out should be altogether erased from the South African Flora. For I. seticulosa was founded upon a specimen collected by Armstrong and doubtfully localised as being from the Cape of Good Hope. But I find it is identical with I. viscosa, Lam., an Australian species, under which I. seticulosa, Harv. must rank as a synonym, the type specimen being identical with Armstrong's No. 385, collected at Port Essington, and doubtless belongs to that gathering.
bibliographicCitation: Multiple authors. 1912. Diagnoses Africanae: XLIX. Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1912(6): 270-283. [https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/42880#page/1/mode/1up] [All rights reserved]

description: E. acuminatum can be separated from E. squarrosum by its much longer, persistent flower bracts that are equal to or longer than the flowers, by the appendages on the standard being above and well free of the auricles and by the presence of golden or russet pubescence especially on the calyx and the undersurface of the leaflets. In E. squarrosum the flower bracts are caducous, shorter than the flower, the pubescence is white and the appendages are better developed extending into the auricles of the standard. From E. rossii C.H.Stirton it differs in its much narrower stipules, larger fruits and pubescence of the leaflets.
bibliographicCitation: Stirton, CH. 1986. The Eriosema squarrosum complex (Papilionoideae, Fabaceae) in southern Africa. Bothalia 16(1): 11-22. [CC BY]

description: Very like I. brachystachya, from which (unless the legumes afford further characters) it chiefly differs in the gland-tipped, rigid setae, mixed with the tomentum of the branches, the flatter and thinner leaflets, and more slender calyx-segments. Leaflets 6-8 lines long, 1.5 line wide, the pairs nearly 1 line apart; the common petiole about quarter inch long.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Leaves with (3)14-41 pairs of pinnae; rhachillae 3.5-9.5 cm long; leaflets in (11)20-48 pairs, 3.5-12 x 0.73 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Ross, JH. 1974. The genus Elephantorrhiza. 11(3): 247-257. [All rights reserved]

description: Peters, Reise Mossamb. Bot. 1 : 9 (1861) is an earlier name for E. goetzei. If this were ever confirmed, then E. petersiana would be the correct name for this species. The holotype of E. petersiana, now destroyed, was a flowering specimen (without leaves) collected by Peters at Sena in Mozambique. Unfortunately the type description is too imperfect to enable the species to be positively identified. Bak.f., Leg. Trop. Afr. 3 : 802 (1930) shed no light on the identity of E. petersiana. Burtt Davy, Fl. Transv. 2 :332 (1932), based his E. (?) sp. nov.? [=E. (?) elongata Burtt Davy ined.] on Burtt Davy H2304 collected at Potgietersrust in the Transvaal. This specimen, which is quite leafless, has istraight immature pods up to 21 x 1.7 cm. The pods of Burtt Davy H2304 resemble those of E. goetzei fairly closely and, although E. goetzei has not been recorded from Potgietersrust subsequently, it seems likely that Burtt Davy's specimen is referable to E. goetzei. E. (?) sp. nov. ? is therefore a probable synonym of E. goetzei.
bibliographicCitation: Ross, JH. 1975. Mimosoideae, Fl. S. Africa 16(1): 1-155. BRI, Pretoria. [CC BY]

description: Eriosema dregei is most commonly confused with E. luteopetalum from which it differs in its silvery stems and immature leaves, narrower wing and keel petals, smaller caducous flower bracts, and the silvery appressed pubescence of the upper surface of the leaflets. In E. luteopetalum the stems and leaves are russet- or golden-brown, the flower bracts are nearly twice as long and wider, and the pubescence on the upper surface of the leaflets is short, appressed and yellowish.
bibliographicCitation: Stirton, CH. 1986. The Eriosema squarrosum complex (Papilionoideae, Fabaceae) in southern Africa. Bothalia 16(1): 11-22. [CC BY]

description: Erect herb; clavate rootstock; naviculate trifoliolate leaves; free, senescent lanceolate-falcate stipules; yellow flowers; caducous flower bract; equal and shortly triangular calyx teeth; standard with bifid hooded appendages free from the auricles and wing petals exceeding the keel blades.
bibliographicCitation: Stirton, CH. 1983. A new species of Eriosema (Fabaceae) from the eastern Transvaal. J. S. African Bot. 49(4): 451-454. [CC BY]

description: E. parviflorum has no close affinities in South Africa. It has often been confused with E. nutans Schinz, but differs from that species in the shape of the standard and the shape of the seeds.
bibliographicCitation: Stirton, CH. 1981. The Eriosema cordatum complex. II. The Eriosema cordatum and E.nutans groups. Bothalia 13(3 & 4): 281-306. [CC BY]

description: The stipules in an Angolan specimen reach 1.7 cm long.
bibliographicCitation: Verdcourt, B. 2001. 61. Leguminosae (Papilionoideae): Tribe 8. Phaseoleae: 62. Eriosema (DC.) Desv., Fl. Zambes. 3(5): 211-242. Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, London. [CC BY]

description: Eriosema populifolium has been much confused with the names Rhynchosia villosa (Meisn.) Druce, R. sigmodes Benth., Eriosema distinctum N.E.Br., and E. cordatum E. Mey. It can be separated from all these taxa by its large incurved connate stipules, together with the shiny, silvery grey pubescence on the surfaces of the leaves and the persistent deep boat-shaped flower bract.

description: Modification in the length of the peduncle relative to that of the subtending leaf, the size of the leaves, and the indumentum on the upper surface of the leaf have led to each form being described as a different species or variety. For example, the form with glabrous and shiny upper leaf surfaces in the Bredasdorp-Caledon area has been described as P. glauca DC. var. biflora E. Mey., and that with small leaves and short peduncles as P. myrtillifolia (Retz.) Willd. var. parvifolia E. Mey. Close examination of these characters, however, shows that they are plastic and would lead to artificial delimitations if separate taxa are retained.

description: E. praeterniissa is most closely related to E. goetzei and to E. elephantina. Both E. goetzei and E. elephantina occur in the eastern Transvaal, but the specimens in question differ from the material of both of these species. E. praeterniissa differs from typical E. goetzei in having consistently fewer pinnae pairs. The leaflets of E. praeterniissa differ from those of E. goetzei in having a somewhat thicker texture and in being ± sessile; the leaflets of typical E. goetzei usually have distinct petiolules. In E. goetzei the pods are long and narrow in proportion to their length (15-44 x 1.3-2.2 cm) and, when mature, the position of the seeds is marked by distinct raised bumps. In E. praeterniissa the pods are shorter and broader (12-18 x 2-3.2 cm), ± compressed, and lack distinct raised bumps over the seeds. The seeds of E. praeterniissa are ± compressed in contrast to the ellipsoid or lenticular seeds of E. goetzei, and they are smaller than those of the latter. Although the length of the racemes provides no discontinuity between the two species, the racemes of E. praeterniissa are consistently short and are much shorter than is usual in E. goetzei. E. praeterniissa differs from E. elephantina in being a robust shrub 1-2 m high and in having branched aerial stems. The leaflets of E. praeterniissa differ slightly in texture and lack the ± conspicuous venation of typical E. elephantina, while the pods tend to be slightly narrower than is usual in E. elephantina.
bibliographicCitation: Ross, JH. 1975. Mimosoideae, Fl. S. Africa 16(1): 1-155. BRI, Pretoria. [CC BY]

description: In general facies V. kokii is very similar to V. mudenia B.J. Pienaar, with the stems and peduncles distinctly alate and the contracted inflorescence bearing two yellow-green flowers, but the leaflets are oblong with rounded base and apex in youth, becoming rhombic or sublobular at maturity. V. kokii is similar to V. richardsiae Verde. (Sect. Microspermae) in having stipules reflexed, connate with the stem but with auricles laterally free; it differs from V. monophylla Taub. (Sect. Haydonia) in the absence of basal glands on the interior whorl of anthers; the style prolongation is reduced to a 'swelling' in the tissue of the style where it bends toward the lateral stigma, as opposed to the 'finger tip' protuberance of V. mudenia and total absence of any prolongation in V. monophylla; the exine sculpture of the pollen grains, appears more rounded than that of V. mudenia as opposed to the total loss thereof in V. monophylla. These characters support the decision to keep it in the same section as V. mudenia but to accept it as a new species. Its distribution also differs from that of V. mudenia.
bibliographicCitation: Pienaar, BJ. 1993. Fabaceae: Vigna kokii, a new species from southern Africa. Bothalia 23(1): 68-70. [CC BY]

description: Compared with Haworthia reinwardtii Haw., it is a smaller plant, has shorter and less acuminate leaves, the face tubercles are in more or less 3 longitudinal rows, and there are more sterile bracts (4-5). description: A virgate shrub, with a good deal of the aspect of P. obliqua, but having different inflorescence, &c. Petioles not half a line long, with minute, fleshy, pubescent stipules. Leaflets an inch long, the medial rather the longest broadly oblong, with cuneate base, conspicuously black-dotted, slightly undulate at the margin. Tufts of flowers hidden among the leaves, on peduncles 1-2 lines long, pedicels equally short. Calyx 14-2 lines long. Legume longer than the calyx.

description: A dwarf, but woody little shrub, 2-4 inches high, densely ramulous and well covered with leaves. Petioles 1 line long. description: Several characters, particularly the structure of the pollen grains, suggest the transference of this species to Nesphostylis is sound, but the facies of the plant is quite different and more closely resembles that of Dolichos, in the affinity of D. trilobus (see Verdcourt, in Kew Bull. 24: 425 (1971)).

description: In South Africa E. buchananii has been confused more often with two other species rather than with E. cordatum. Here it has been known under the name E. nutans Schinz [= E. polystachyum (A. Rich.) Bak.] to which it has a very strong resemblance, and also to E. montanum Bak. f. which does not extend as far south as South Africa. E. buchananii may be readily separated from the rest of the complex by the the middle of an oblong standard, the large incurved flattened auricles and the falcate stipules with the base narrower than the middle. The appendage is characteristic as it is divided into two shallow, crescentiform ridges which lie closely one on either side of the central axis of the standard. E. nutans is separated by its smaller auricles and its undivided appendage which occurs just above the auricles merging into them.
bibliographicCitation: Stirton, CH. 1981. The Eriosema cordatum complex. II. The Eriosema cordatum and E.nutans groups. Bothalia 13(3 & 4): 281-306. [CC BY]

description: Over 50 specimens had been incorrectly named in the past. This material had been referred to E. psoraleoides (E. cajanoides), E. parviflorum, E. zeyheri and E. squarrosum. E. psoraleoides with its very small stipules, wide obovate standard without appendages, different keels, wings and pistil is easily separated from E. nutans which has an oblong standard with appendages and long lanceolate stipules. The two species differ also in that in E. nutans the peduncle is longer than half the length of the inflorescence. In E. psoraleoides the peduncle is less than one third the length of the inflorescence. E. parviflorum is distinguishable from E. nutans by its wide obovate (1.2: 1) standard, and its allopatric distribution (almost restricted to Natal in S. Africa).
bibliographicCitation: Stirton, CH. 1981. The Eriosema cordatum complex. II. The Eriosema cordatum and E.nutans groups. Bothalia 13(3 & 4): 281-306. [CC BY]

description: It is readily distinguished from this species by its rhizomatous underground system, the presence of persistent acrorachial stipels, the general shape of the flower parts, the length of the fruits and the exerted stigma.
bibliographicCitation: Stirton, CH; Gordon-Gray, KDH. 1978. The Eriosema cordatum complex I. The Eriosema populifolium group. Bothalia 12(3): 395-404. [CC BY]

description: Eriosema gunniae was first collected near Pilgrims Rest in 1915. It has been commonly referred to E. cordatum, but can be distinguished by its stigma ex-serted from the staminal sheath and by its persistent flower bract that approximates the length of the flower. Four collections are included temporarily in E. gunniae: Young All from Middelburg, Young A214 from Susterstroom, Rudatis 2513 from Tautes-berg and Grobelaar 1675 from Steenkampbergen. This composite group occurs to the west of the range of E. gunniae sensu stricto. Further collections from the intervening areas may enable their correct status to be decided.
bibliographicCitation: Stirton, CH. 1981. Studies in the Leguminosae-Papilionoideae of southern Africa. Bothalia 13(3 & 4): 317-325. [CC BY]

description: Eriosema latifolium is closely allied to E. dregei and E. luteopetalum, two other yellow-flowered suffrutices from the same general region. It differs from these two species in its much smaller flowers, the appendages on the standard being well-free of the auricles, its shorter stipules and narrowly oblong racemes.
bibliographicCitation: Stirton, CH. 1986. The Eriosema squarrosum complex (Papilionoideae, Fabaceae) in southern Africa. Bothalia 16(1): 11-22. [CC BY]

description: This species is easily separated from E. cordatum by its free stipules. In areas where the two species overlap there exist plants which may be intermediates. Such plants, because they have free stipules, are included here in E. lucipetum. They tend to have pale pink and yellow flowers (for example Stirton 1416). Further studies may indicate that they are hybrids.
bibliographicCitation: Stirton, CH. 1981. The Eriosema cordatum complex. II. The Eriosema cordatum and E.nutans groups. Bothalia 13(3 & 4): 281-306. [CC BY]

description: Its nearest allies are E. latifolium and E. dregei from which it differs in its very much larger flowers and distinctive pubescence.
bibliographicCitation: Stirton, CH. 1986. The Eriosema squarrosum complex (Papilionoideae, Fabaceae) in southern Africa. Bothalia 16(1): 11-22. [CC BY]

description: A slender but rigid, straight-branched shrub, 1-2 feet high, with green (not hoary) foliage and thinly strigillose. Common petiole not half inch long; leaflets 3-5 lines long, in a. rounded at point, in b. more or less acute. Peduncles slender, very short. Flowers like those of I. zeyheri. Legumes 1-1.5 inch long, many-seeded, at first strigillose, then glabrescent.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: This species has been consistently lumped with E. squarrosum, E. dregei, E. latifolium and E. luteopetalum. It differs from all of these species in its red and yellow flowers and golden-haired calyces; occasional yellow morphs can occur. The latter species all have yellow flowers and silver-haired calyces. From E. preptum it can be separated by its much larger flowers and fruits and by the wing petals exceeding the keel petals.
bibliographicCitation: Stirton, CH. 1986. The Eriosema squarrosum complex (Papilionoideae, Fabaceae) in southern Africa. Bothalia 16(1): 11-22. [CC BY]

description: A densely branched, strong bush, 1-2 feet high; branches and twigs erect, densely leafy. Leaves either exactly digitate on an obsolete petiole, or obliquely and imperfectly digitate on a little longer petiole. Leaflets 3-7 lines long, scarcely a line wide, with thickened and recurved margins. Flowers pinky-purple, very minutely downy, 2-2.5 lines long. Legumes uncial, when ripe quite glabrous. This has much the aspect of I. brachystachya, but the leaves are digitate, not pinnate; and the legumes glabrous not tomentose.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Stem 2-3 feet high, straight and rod-like, pale brown, minutely puberalous, somewhat panicled above; twigs slender, erecto-patent, subsimple, 5-8 inches long. Leaves nearly an inch apart, recurvo-patent; the common petiole 0.25-0.75 inch long. Leaflets 4-5 lines long, 1-1.5 line wide, pale. Racemes loosely many flowered, 2-3 inches long; pedicels longish. Calyx very small, white-hairy. Petals 4-5 lines long, dark brown externally. Legumes not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Harvey, WH. 1862. Leguminosae. In: WH Harvey & OW Sonder (eds), Leguminosae to Loranthaceae, Fl. Cap. (Harvey) 2: 1-285. Lovell Reeve & Co. Ltd., London. [https://doi.org/10.5962/bhl.title.821] [All rights reserved]

description: Stems 12-18 inches high, ascending, filiform. Petioles 1.5-2 inches long. Leaflets shorter or longer, the lower broader and blunter, the upper very narrow, acute at each end. Peduncles 4-6 inches long, the upper half floriferous; the raceme lengthening as the flowers expand. Bracts ovate-oblong, with a long, narrow point. Flowers small.

description: L. contaminata differs from L. longipes in having a more decumbent habit, the presence of a leaf articulation, wing petals that are as long as or longer than the keel petal and stipitatefruit (stipe 5-18 mm long). L. longipes has a diffuse habit, leaf articulations are absent, the wing petals are invariably shorter than the keel petal and the fruit is long stipitate (stipe 12-55 mm long).
bibliographicCitation: Le Roux, MM; Van Wyk, B-E. 2008. A revision of Lebeckia sect. Lebeckia: The L. plukenetiana group (Fabaceae, Crotalarieae). S. African J. Bot. 74: 660-676. description: L. gracilis is similar to L. ambigua but differs in its calyx that is ±equally lobed and with the lobes shorter than the tube (calyx subequally lobed and the lobes as long as the tube in L. ambigua) (. L. gracilis also differs from L. ambigua in its shorter and more congested racemes. The two species are allopatric.
bibliographicCitation: Le Roux, MM; Van Wyk, B-E. 2007. A revision of Lebeckia sect. Lebeckia: The L. sepiaria group. S. African J. Bot. 73: 118-130. [Copyright held by the South African Association of Botanists (2007); http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/journal/02546299] [CC BY]

description: L. grandiflora is similar to L. pauciflora in the long calyx lobes, obovate wing petals, stipitate fruit and habit, but differs in the invariably articulated leaves, the straight keel, and the shorter, thin-walled, membranous fruits, 60 to 77 mm long. In L. pauciflora, western populations have articulated leaves and eastern populations have unarticulated leaves, the keel is twisted, and the spongy fruit is 70 to 165 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Le Roux, MM; Van Wyk, B-E. 2009. A revision of Lebeckia sect. Lebeckia: The L. pauciflora and L. wrightii groups (Fabaceae, Crotalariaea). S. African J. Bot. 75: 83-96. description: L. longipes differs from L. pauciflora in the absence of a leaf articulation, calyx teeth that are as long as the calyx tube and long, stipitate, flat fruit. In some populations ofL. pauciflora, the leaves are not articulated (OTU 3). The calyx teeth are longer than the calyx tube (up to twice as long) and the fruit is short-stipitate and semi-terete in L. pauciflora. description: L. meyeriana is closely related to L. plukenetiana, but differs in the presence of leaf articulations, wing petals that are shorter than the keel petal and oblong, straight fruit. In contrast, L. plukenetiana has no leaf articulations, the wing petals are always longer than the keel petal and the fruit is narrowly oblong to oblong, straight or falcate. Lebeckia macowanii (OTU 3) has exactly the same fruit and flower structure as the typical form of the species but the flowers and fruits are one and a half times larger. However, the presence of intermediates (e.g. Lewis 472, SAM) suggest that L. macowanii is merely one extreme of the range of variation in the species.

description: L. pauciflora is similar to L. wrightii in both having a twisted keel, calyx lobes that are longer than the calyx tube and obovate wings, but differs in the erect, perennial habit, absence of stipules, absence of hair (except on the inside of the calyx tips) and long, terete fruit (70-165 mm long). L. wrightii is a hairy, decumbent annual or short-lived fireweed, with stipulate leaves and sessile, flat fruit (23-35 mm long). L. pauciflora is also similar to L. grandiflora as both species have long calyx lobes, obovate wing petals, stipitate fruit and a sub-erect to decumbent habit, but differs in details of the leaf, fruit and keel.

description: R. amplexicaulis differs from R. acuminata in that the leaves may also be reniform (not only cordate, as in R. acuminata) and are often pale green (dark green to glaucous in R. acuminata). R. amplexicaulis also differs from R-acuminata in the shape of the standard petal which is broadly ovate or broadly elliptic in the former and elliptic or suborbicular in the latter. R. amplexicaulis differs from the remaining species in the reticulate, cordate to reniform leaves and the pod shape, as well as the absence of bracteoles.

description: R crispa is similar to R. lancea but differs in the larger, distinctly penninerved leaves (venation indistinct in R. lancea), which have markedly crisped margins (margins not crisped in R. lancea), the basal leaves which are shorter and broader than the upper leaves (basal leaves are slightly shorter than but as broad as the upper leaves in R. lancea), the smaller flowers and the calyx in which the lateral sinus is shallower and narrower than the other sinuses (the lateral lobes do not appear to be paired, however, as in R. lancea). In R. crispa, the carinal calyx lobe is shorter than the others (as long as the others in R. lancea), the standard blade ovate (elliptic or round in R. lancea), the petal claws are shorter than in R. lancea, the wing apex is obovate (obtuse in R. lancea), the ovary narrowly ovate (± oblong in R. lancea) and the style is strongly upcurved (basally down-curved, distally upcurved in R. lancea).

description: R diffusa is distinguished from the other species of section Colobotropis by the coppice leaves which are different in size and shape from the upper leaves, the very small flowers (similar in size to R. spicata and some forms of R. capensis subsp. capensis), the round standard b'ade and the invariable presence of wing sculpturing. It also differs from R. capensis in the softer-textured flowers (the lowers are usually tougher-textured in R. capensis), the keel shape which is usually obtuse or rarely ± truncate (distinctly truncate in R. capensis), the very small calyx which is usually much shorter than the corolla (calyx larger in R. capensis and not as much shorter than the corolla) and the very variable leaf shape (more variable than in R. capensis).
bibliographicCitation: Campbell, GJ; Van Wyk, B-E. 2001. A taxonomic revision of Rafnia (Fabaceae, Crotalarieae). S. African J. Bot. 67: 90-149. [Copyright held by the South African Association of Botanists (2001); http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/journal/02546299] [CC BY]

description: R. ovata is recognised by the herbaceous stems which are not much-branched, the acuminate leaf apices (the basal leaves are often very large, comparable in size to those of R. triflora), the inflorescence, which is subtended by highly reduced opposite leaves that often appear to be absent, the large flowers, the calyx lobes that are shorter than the calyx tube and the large and stipitate pods that are broadly winged on the upper suture.
bibliographicCitation: Campbell, GJ; Van Wyk, B-E. 2001. A taxonomic revision of Rafnia (Fabaceae, Crotalarieae). S. African J. Bot. 67: 90-149. [Copyright held by the South African Association of Botanists (2001); http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/journal/02546299] [CC BY]

description: R. spicata is similar to R. capensis subsp. capensis (particularly the Ceres form, from which it is frequently difficult to distinguish), but differs in the inflorescences which are often secondarily aggregated towards the branch ends into spike-like flowering branches (inflorescences not aggregated in subsp. capensis), the smaller, softer-textured flowers and the wing petals which may or may not be sculptured (sculpturing invariably absent in subsp. capensis). It also differs from R. diffusa in the smaller, procumbent, mat-like habit (diffuse and much-branched in R. diffusa).

description: Fruit an indehiscent nutlet with a compressed stipe 3-3.5 mm long; upper crest only 0.6-1.1 mm broad; lower parts not wing-like; body of fruit 7-11 x 6-8.5 mm (excl. stipe and style), rather turgid, hard, strongly reticulate on the sides, the veins or ridges not (or hardly) organized into a zigzag ridge.

description: The variation in the species is considerable. The other extremes, viz. forms with short, deltoid calyx lobes and broad subglabrous leaflets, occur in the Gydo Pass region of the Ceres Division. A few suspected hybrids between A. rugosa and A. linearifolia are known from the region of Saron, Tulbagh Division, and also from Stettynskloof and Du Toit's Kloof, Worcester Division. This species was united with Aspalathus linearifolia DC by Dahlgren, and this may be justified on the basis of some intermediates (Ladismith Division) and some possible hybrids(e.g. in Tulbagh Division). However, considering the distinctness in most of the distribution area the species are here treated as separate.

description: L. wrightii is closely allied to L. uniflora, and both are annual pyrophytes with pubescent leaves and calyces, but differs in the few-flowered inflorescences (up to five flowers per inflorescence), and smaller flowers (5-8 mm long) with shorter wings (6.5-9.0 mm long). L. uniflora has single-flowered inflorescences, and larger flowers (8-12 mm long) with wings 11.5-15.0 mm long. L. wrightii is also similar to L. pauciflora in the wing and keel petal structure, but differs in the few- flowered inflorescence, decumbent habit (annual fireweed) the emarginate apex of the standard petal, the short, sessile, pubescent fruit, and the small, mottled black and white seeds. L. pauciflora is many-flowered, it is a virgate, suffrutex, the standard petal has an obtuse apex, the fruit is long, stipitate and glabrous and the seeds are large, pink-brown and mottled dark brown.

Densely tubercled leaves occur on the Swartberg and Riviersonderend Mountains, while forms in the Swellendam-Robertson Divisions (Langeberg) have smoother, glabrous leaves, bracts and calyx lobes. Indistinctly tubercled leaves also characterize the forms in the Worcester Division (Stettynsberg) and those on the Potberg in Bredasdorp Division, the latter with a very short, incurved standard cusp, rather like that in some forms of A. spicata.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Differs from A. ciliaris in the simple bracts and soft, slightly flat leaflets on the young branches (A. ciliaris in the same region is represented by forms quite unlike A. confusa). Perhaps closest to A. spicata, but different from this, too, in the leaflet shape.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: A. cymbiformis is similar to and probably most closely related to A. linguiloba, A. keeromsbergensis and A. incana. An intermediate between A. cymbiformis and A. linguiloba is Esterhuysen 19574 from Bredasdorp Poort, Bredasdorp Division. It is best included in A. linguiloba.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Distinct from A. salteri in its prostrate habit, flat and ovate bracts and bracteoles and flat, ovate calyx lobes. Probably related to A. salteri and A. pallescens.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Differs from A. prostrata in being procumbent or decumbent rather than prostrate and in having succulent, subterete bracts, bracteoles and calyx lobes. A. salteri, A. prostrata and A. pallescens are probably rather closely related to each other and all three to A. cymbiformis.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: A very distinct species, ecologically characteristic in being calcicolous. Perhaps closely related to the equally calcicolous A. prostrata and A. salteri, but very different in habit.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: A. muraltioides is closely allied to A. hispida, A. puberula and A. ericifolia.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Characteristic in having a glabrous, often orange or ferruginous (to purple) keel, straight, spreading leaflets with short, spreading pubescence, and small bracts and bracteoles. Otherwise similar to the species around A. ericifolia. The most closely related species probably are A. puberul aand A. rectistyla.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: A very characteristic species, unusual in the genus by the prolonged keel and nearly straight style. Obviously most similar to A. puberula and A. flexuosa.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: R. crassifolia is distinguished from the other species of Rafnia by the somewhat succulent, often bright green leaves which have red margins, the inflorescence which lacks a peduncle or pseudopeduncle, the elongated Pedicels (about as long as the flowers) and the subpanduriform standard petal which tapers into the claw.
bibliographicCitation: Campbell, GJ; Van Wyk, B-E. 2001. A taxonomic revision of Rafnia (Fabaceae, Crotalarieae). S. African J. Bot. 67: 90-149. [Copyright held by the South African Association of Botanists (2001); http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/journal/02546299] [CC BY]

description: R. elliptica is similar to R. vlokii but differs in longer pedicels, the smaller calyx, the broader carinal lobe which is about as long as the other lobes (not very narrow and shorter than the other lobes in R. vlokii), the basal callosities on the standard petal (basal callosities absent in R vlokii), the broadly convex lower margin of the wing petal (margin more or less straight in R vlokii), the style that is shorter than the ovary (about as along as the ovary in R vlokii), the obliquely lanceolate pods (obliquely oblanceolate in R. vlokii) and the smaller seeds which have a smooth testa (seeds with a striate testa in R. vlokii). R. elliptica also differs from R. alata in the much larger size and presence of a ridge between the upper lobes on the calyx tube (wing-like extensions between all the lobes in R. alata).
bibliographicCitation: Campbell, GJ; Van Wyk, B-E. 2001. A taxonomic revision of Rafnia (Fabaceae, Crotalarieae). S. African J. Bot. 67: 90-149. [Copyright held by the South African Association of Botanists (2001); http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/journal/02546299] [CC BY]

description: A. parviflora is extraordinary in lacking both bract and bracteoles. Otherwise it shows several similarities to A. hispida and A. ericifolia.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: R. lancea is distinguished from all the other species of Rafnia by the calyx in which the upper and lateral lobes are fused higher up in pairs on either side, the long petal claws, which are rather long relative to the petal blades in comparison with the other species, the curvature of the style, which is proximally downcurved and distally upcurved and the proximally curved pod.
bibliographicCitation: Campbell, GJ; Van Wyk, B-E. 2001. A taxonomic revision of Rafnia (Fabaceae, Crotalarieae). S. African J. Bot. 67: 90-149. [Copyright held by the South African Association of Botanists (2001); http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/journal/02546299] [CC BY]

description: R. triflora is recognised by its often subtriangular, cordate-based upper leaves which are closely appressed to the stem, the very large, elliptic to round basal leaves and the inflorescences in which three single-flowered racemes emerge from the leaf axils, giving the appearance of a 3-flowered inflorescence.
bibliographicCitation: Campbell, GJ; Van Wyk, B-E. 2001. A taxonomic revision of Rafnia (Fabaceae, Crotalarieae). S. African J. Bot. 67: 90-149. [Copyright held by the South African Association of Botanists (2001); http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/journal/02546299] [CC BY]

description: Samara obliquely oval or circular, usually 12.5-17.5 x 8.5-12 mm in size.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1975. Studies on Wiborgia Thunb. and related species of Lebeckia Thunb. (Fabaceae). Opera Bot. 38: 1-83. [All rights reserved]

description: A. pinea is most similar to A. willdenowiana and A. uniflora, but also approaches A. macrocarpa.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: The species obviously approaches most closely A. rostrata, though superficially more resembling A. pinea and A. willdenowiana.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: The appearance of the flowers resembles that of A. bracteata and related species, that of subgenus Nortieria and of other species groups and may be basic in the genus. The species is quite distinct by the numerous ovules and linear pods.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: This species is obviously most closely related to A. polycephala, from which it differs in the glabrous leaves and bracts, and the more numerous ovules.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Obviously close to A. fasciculata, A. rupestris, A. venosa and A. polycephala, all with the lowest calyx lobe enlarged and with many other shared features.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Distinguished by the short-velvety calyx with rather short, ovate lobes. Otherwise obviously close to A. verbasciformis and A. acanthes.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Strongly reminiscent of, but with less enlarged median calyx lobe than A. suaveolens and A. fasciculata on the Great Winterhoek Mountain.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: The similarity in petal shape with A. esterhuysenia suggests a close relationship.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Similar to A. sceptrum-aureu and A. verbasciformis but distinct by the tomentose calyx and 8-11 mm long calyx lobes.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Obviously closely related to A. shawii, which was included in it by Dahlgren. In its beaked keel it also slightly resembles A. pinea and A. rostrata (convergent evolution ?), but differs in the 2-ovulate ovary and other details, and also A. vulpina which has, however, flat, broad leaflets.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: The species is closely allied to A. inops and the delimitation between these species is doubtful (note that A. stenophylla subsp. garciana has here been transferred to A. inops). These species are allied to A. aspalathoides, A. marginata, A. psoraleoides and A. cytisoides.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Breadth and shape of the leaflets are variable: from suborbicular to narrowly ovate or rhombic, the latter often petiolate and more sharply spine-tipped; the forms with broadest leaflets are from the Elim region, Bredasdorp Division.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Resembling in habit A. kougaensis rather than A. hystrix but like the latter of these species, it has a glabrous keel; differing from A. hystrix in the weaker leaves and the short, more velutinous calyx and calyx lobes. Its distinctness from A. hystrix needs, however, to be verified.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: The forms in the Worcester Division ('A. sphaerocephala') have linear, narrow leaflets rarely more than 1.5 mm broad, whereas those of the Tulbagh region have leaflets (on long-shoots) 2-6 mm broad. The previous distinction into subsp. truncata and subsp. sphaerocephala (Schltr.) Dahlg. hardly seems warranted.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Like A. hirta but leaves grey-hairy.
bibliographicCitation: Boatwright, JS; et al. 2019. Fabaceae. In: CL Bredenkamp (ed.), A Flora of the Eastern Cape Province, Strelitzia 41(2): 926-1066. South African National Biodiversity Institute, Pretoria. [CC BY]

description: Distinct by the rostrate sericeous keel, the short calyx lobes and the spiny, A. hirta-like habit. Probably most closely allied to A. teres and A. spectabilis.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: The outpost at Bain's Kloof, Worcester Division, has much shorter pedicels (1-2 mm) than have the other forms (4-5 mm), and also has a broader oblong (rather than linear) bract. It was described by Dahlgren as subsp. crassa R.Dahlgren and may deserve recognition, although this is not yet quite clear.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: This geographically rather restricted species with a limited morphological variation was described as several separate new species by Ecklon & Zeyher. In fact it agrees in most respects with A. chortophila (syn. A. hilaris), although A. intermedia has considerably smaller flowers and is thus technically easy to distinguish, but may not merit species rank.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Probably closely related to A. alopecurus, but with much shorter calyx lobes, shorter calyx pubescence, and differently shaped keel blade. Probably close also to A. setacea, but without apical standard cusp and with subterete calyx lobes.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: The species is closely related to A. rugosa, with which it intergrades and probably hybridizes. It is also very similar to A. bidouwensis.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: This species resembles A. carnosa in most features but is larger and coarser in all parts.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: This species and A. salicifolia, which are obviously closely related to each other, in spite of the different habit, may be most closely allied to A. aspalathoides.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Obviously most closely related to A. carnosa and A. excelsa. This is indicated by the carnose petals, rostrate keel and the bracts which are accreted to the pedicel.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: There is great variation in floral size, degree of thickness, flatness and sharpness of the leaflets, and of fusion of bract base with pedicel. The species is undoubtedly most closely related to A. subulata from which it differs in the glabrous calyx tube.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Distinct by the strong, knotty branches, the very small clustered leaflets, and the floral heads. Partly confused with A. sericea, A. aemula, A. altissima and A. caledonensis.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: A. callosa is closely related to A. tylodes and differs from this in having glabrous branches and somewhat larger flowers. These two species are obviously rather isolated in the genus.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Similar to, but smaller than, A. aciphylla; especially the narrower calyx and smaller fruits are important differences. The flowers and their petals are also narrower than those of A. collina.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: The species approaches both A. ramulosa, with three equally large leaflets, and A. aemula and A. sericea with one large central and two reduced to absent lateral leaflets per long-shoot leaf.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: A very distinctive species approaching A. sulphurea, A. citrina and A. arida, but with ± pedunculate inflorescences on the lateral branchlets (the other species have solitary flowers on lateral short-shoots).
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Related to A. lotoides but different in the non-silvery leaves, the sparser and more elongate spikes, the recurved calyx lobes and the more intensely yellow petals. It is not quite clear to which other species these two are most closely related, although a close affinity with A. tridentata, A. quinquefolia is possible.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Allied to A. pachyloba and A. pallidiflora, differing from both in the rose-coloured petals and broader, spathulate bracts.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: The species shows an interesting variation in the form of a geographical cline, the southern forms having short, deltoid calyx lobes 1-2 mm long, and rather short bracts and calyx lobes; all these become successively longer towards the north, the forms of the Clanwilliam and Piketberg Divisions having linear calyx lobes ±10 mm long, and long slender leaves. The branches of the northern forms also have longer, more spreading branches. Leaf base spurs occur only in the southern forms. A. ternata and A. dasyantha are closely allied. Their connection with other species with flat leaflets is uncertain, but they are possibly closest to A. intervallaris or A. tridentata.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Distinct by the shorter, green, sparsely hairy or glabrous leaves and the woolly calyx. The species is also more rigid and knotty than A. ternata.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Incompletely known as regards the closest connections; perhaps A. intricata, which has longer bracteoles and calyx lobes and shorter petal claws (stages comparable?), perhaps A. lactea, with less pubescent standard and much less thorny branches.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Similar to A. caledonensis but with puberulous pubescence, ovate calyx lobes and smaller, somewhat different petals. Probably most closely related to A. quadrata.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: A morphologically isolated species with a peculiar combination of characters: rod-like stem (like A. caledonensis), lanceolate leaves (like those of A. aspalathoides) and flowers with a rostrate calyx (as in A. willdenowiana).
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: A. subtingens is undoubtedly closely related to A. lactea, A. petersonii and A. leucophylla.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Closely allied to A. bodkinii, but possibly also to A. tridentata subsp. fragilis.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Distinct by the green foliage, larger petals and spicate inflorescence. The shoot system and inflorescence agree with that of A. lanata and A. latifolia, but the habit and floral details with A. bodkinii.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Closely related to A. spinosa subsp. glauca which has similar flat, broad leaflets. As A. spinosa subsp. glauca occurs far from A. obtusata and has larger flowers and recurved, short lateral thorns (as most forms of subsp. spinosa), is seems probable that the flat leaflets have evolved independently in this and in A. obtusata.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]

description: Larger in total size than all western forms of A. spinosa; resembling A. glabrata in size, but with grey-pubescent foliage and calyx and with longer, more woolly pods.
bibliographicCitation: Dahlgren, RMT. 1988. Papilionoideae: Crotalarieae (Aspalathus), Fl. S. Africa 16(3,6): 1-430. BRI, Pretoria. [http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209549#page/1/mode/1up] [CC BY]
